AC: Alternating current; current that changes direction.
B+: The positive high-voltage supply used by the tube circuits.
B_MAIN: The supply node that feeds the output-transformer centre tap.
B_RAW: The rectified supply node before the standby switch.
B_SCREEN: The filtered supply node for the output-tube screen grids.
B_PRE: The filtered supply node for the specified preamplifier stages.
B_EARLY: The filtered supply node for the earlier preamplifier stages.
Bias: A steady voltage or current that sets a device operating point.
Bleeder: A resistor used to remove capacitor charge; its presence alone does not prove safe residual voltage.
Brownout: A supply-voltage reduction below the normal operating range.
Bypass capacitor: A capacitor that provides a short local path for changing current.
Capacitance: The ratio of stored charge to voltage; measured in farads (F).
Capacitor: A component that stores charge and electrical energy.
Cassette: A removable assembly carrying the electronics and its supports.
Chassis: The metal structure that supports and encloses the electronics.
Chuck: The drill part that grips the bit.
Clearance: The shortest distance through air between conductive parts.
Common-mode voltage: Voltage shared by conductors relative to a specified reference.
Creepage: The shortest path along an insulating surface between conductive parts.
CT: Centre tap; an electrical connection part-way along a transformer winding.
Datum: A fixed point, line or surface used as the measurement reference.
DC: Direct current; current that flows in one direction.
Derating: Operating below a component rating to allow for heat or other specified conditions.
Dissipation: Electrical energy converted to heat per unit time; measured in watts (W).
DRC: Design Rule Check; a PCB geometry and connectivity check.
EMI: Electromagnetic interference; unwanted electrical or magnetic coupling.
Envelope: The space occupied by a part or assembly, including stated allowances.
ERC: Electrical Rules Check; a schematic consistency check.
Faraday shield: A conductive shield used against electric-field coupling; it does not guarantee low-frequency magnetic shielding.
Feedback: A signal returned from an output to an earlier stage to control gain or response.
Flange: A projecting edge used to attach or stiffen a part.
Functional block: A group of parts with one defined job and specified connections to other groups.
GB1: The design identifier for the declared signal-ground to chassis connection.
Ground: A named circuit reference; it is not automatically protective earth.
Ground loop: A closed conducting path between ground connections that can carry unwanted current.
Harness: A grouped set of wires, contacts and connectors.
Headroom: The signal margin before clipping or another specified limit.
Heater: The tube element that heats the cathode.
Heater reference: The voltage used to set the heater circuit relative to the tube cathodes.
Heater-to-cathode voltage: The voltage between a tube heater and cathode; it must stay within the tube limits.
HREF: The design name for the heater reference node.
HV: High voltage; use the actual voltage and insulation requirement in each design check.
ICM: Interpretable Context Methodology; the project structure that records ownership, inputs, outputs and checks.
Impedance: Opposition to alternating current, including resistance and frequency-dependent effects; measured in ohms (Ω).
Inrush: The brief current rise when power is applied.
KaTeX: The software used to display mathematical notation in these HTML documents.
Lead: A component terminal that connects to the board.
Lead protrusion: The length of a component lead below the board.
Load: The circuit or device that takes current from a source.
Loop resistance: The total resistance of the supply and return conductors, contacts and terminations.
Net: A named set of electrically connected points.
Node: An electrical connection shared by specified components.
Nominal: The stated reference value before tolerance and operating variation.
PE: Protective earth; the protective connection to exposed conductive parts.
Pin map: A table assigning each connector contact to a circuit node and function.
Preamp: Preamplifier; the stages that prepare the input signal for the power amplifier.
Qualification: Checks that show a design meets stated limits under stated conditions.
RC time constant: Resistance multiplied by capacitance for a simple resistor-capacitor model; not a safe service delay.
Rectifier: A circuit that changes alternating current into current of one polarity.
Reservoir: A capacitor bank that stores energy after rectification.
Return path: The route that carries current back to its source.
Ripple: Periodic supply variation remaining after rectification and filtering.
Screen grid: An electrode in the output tube supplied from the screen supply.
Schematic: A drawing of electrical connections and component functions.
Series: Connected in sequence so the same branch current passes through each part.
Parallel: Connected across the same two electrical nodes.
Skin effect: Current crowding near a conductor surface as frequency increases.
Socket: A replaceable connection that holds a tube or integrated circuit.
Standby: A switch state; it does not by itself prove the amplifier is de-energized.
Strain relief: A support that keeps cable forces away from electrical terminations.
Swarf: Metal chips left by drilling or cutting.
Tolerance: The permitted variation from a specified value.
Transformer: A magnetic device that transfers energy between windings.
Winding: A coil of insulated wire in a transformer or inductor.
Wet/dry: The balance between the effect signal and the unaffected signal.
K1: The candidate with the bulk and screen supply below and stage filters above.
K2: The upper power-assembly reference layout; it is not yet a proven fit.
K4: The candidate with all power-supply filters below.
Gate: A checkpoint that requires specified evidence before the next activity.
Prototype: A test assembly used to check the design before release.
Residual voltage: Voltage still present after power removal or disconnection.
Stored energy: Energy held in a charged capacitor; it depends on capacitance and voltage.
Dummy load: A resistor assembly that absorbs amplifier output power in place of a speaker during electrical tests.
Sense resistor: A known resistor used to calculate current from its measured voltage drop.
Oscilloscope: An instrument that displays voltage against time.
Differential probe: A probe that measures voltage between two points within its specified differential and earth-referenced voltage limits.
Attenuator: A circuit that reduces a signal to a specified level.
Clipping: Signal flattening when the amplifier reaches its output limit.
Parasitic: An unintended electrical effect caused by physical conductors, parts or layout.
Insulation resistance: Resistance through an insulating path, measured at a specified test voltage.
Protective bond: The intentional protective-earth connection to exposed conductive metal.
Frequency response: How gain and phase change with signal frequency.
Impedance sweep: An impedance measurement repeated across a specified range of frequencies.
Cathode: The tube electrode that emits electrons when heated.
Cathode follower: A tube stage that takes its signal output from the cathode.
Divider: Series components that produce a fraction of an applied voltage.
THD: Total harmonic distortion; harmonic content relative to the fundamental, using the stated harmonic range.
Fundamental: The waveform component at the applied signal frequency.
Timestep: The time interval used by the simulator to resolve a waveform.
Transient: A change in circuit conditions over time, such as startup or shutdown.
Stiff supply: A modeled voltage source whose voltage does not change with load.
Corner: A selected combination of component and operating limits.
